rationale: The observed prefix ends a sentence-initial prepositional phrase (“In a little village,”), but the model strongly favors a period because its noun-final period rule has very high weight; the comma root has little applicable mass. Add a comma rule for the reusable pattern of a space followed by a preposition, determiner, optional adjectives, and a noun. This also expresses the introductory-phrase structure in examples such as “On a sunny day,” without conditioning on a particular place or name. A noun-final period remains valid in other contexts, and prepositional phrases need not always be introductory or comma-terminated, so the rule is limited to the sentence-boundary-like space plus phrase pattern. This is a provisional repair; replay behavior still needs the gate’s evaluation.
